summary: Gone Clatsop County lookout: tower built 1940 on ridge south of summit, pole tower 1955, emergency-only from 1960s, reportedly burned after a planned museum move.

facts.design: 1940 tower; L-4 cab added 1951; pole L-4 tower from 1955 (40 ft per FFLOS, 50 ft wooden per firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: Gone. Keith Argow (Ph.D., CF) says the tower was taken apart and burned around the time of a planned move to the Camp 18 owner's museum

events.note: Tower built on the ridgetop about 1.5 miles south of the summit
L-4 cab added to the tower
Photo caption: lookout painted by Fire Warden Richard Spray and crew; the woman on the right was the lookout
40-foot pole L-4 tower replaced the tower and cab (firelookout.com says 50-foot wooden tower)
Used for emergencies only; source says beginning in the 1960s, so the year is approximate
Registered November 17, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: tower built here in 1940; L-4 cab added 1951; 40-foot pole L-4 tower replaced them in 1955 on the ridge 1.5 miles south of the summit
evidence.quote: A tower was built here in 1940, an L-4 cab was added in 1951, and a 40' pole L-4 tower replaced these in 1955 1.5 miles south of the summit on the ridgetop.

evidence.supports: firelookout.com timeline: 1940 tower, 1955 50-foot wooden tower, ridge 1.5 miles south of summit, emergency use 1960s, gone
evidence.quote: 1940: tower. 1955: 50' wooden ODF tower. 1.5 miles south of summit on ridgetop. Emergency 1960s. Gone.

evidence.supports: administered by Oregon Department of Forestry
1952 lookout painted by Fire Warden Richard Spray and crew; the lady on the right was the lookout
evidence.quote: In 1952, the lookout was freshly painted by Fire Warden Richard Spray and his crew. The lady on the right was the lookout.

evidence.supports: used for emergencies only from the 1960s; now gone
evidence.quote: It was used for emergencies only beginning in the 1960s and is now gone.

evidence.supports: owner of Camp 18 wanted the tower for a museum
evidence.quote: The logger owner of Camp 18 had contacted ODF to get it for his museum.

evidence.supports: a helicopter company agreed to airlift the tower
evidence.quote: Columbia Helicopters who agreed to airlift it

evidence.supports: tower taken apart and burned in the same period
evidence.quote: Unfortunately in the same time period it was taken apart and burned.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS register says the 1955 tower was a 40-foot pole tower (about 12.2 m); firelookout.com says 50-foot wooden tower (15.2 m). The record's 15.2 m was kept because it matches firelookout.com; the story reports both figures.

notes_for_editor: Only two short source pages describe the tower. Height is disputed (40 ft FFLOS vs 50 ft firelookout.com). The burning rests on one first-person account (Keith Argow) with no year, so no burned or removed event was entered. The 1952 staffing event rests on a photo caption. No source describes the site today. The oregonlookouts.weebly.com index gave no Wickiup detail. The record's coordinate conflict (west_us_lookouts 46.1056, -123.58624) was not checked.
